title: Convert some tvb_new_subset_length_caplen -> tvb_new_subset_length
description:
tvb_new_subset_length(tvb, offset, reported_length) sets the
subset TVB's captured_length to
MIN(tvb_captured_length_remaining(tvb, offset), reported_length)

so dissectors don't need to do that themselves and can call
the non caplen function.

Get rid of the commonly used idiom in a number of dissectors.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 1f2f2e55 - Convert some tvb_new_subset_length_caplen -> tvb_new_subset_length
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22211/diffs?diff_id=1556343526&start_sha=253f076db843452805f3b68da414b2cfe4430481)

By changing the `tvb_new_subset_length_caplen` to `tvb_new_subset_length`, it no longer immediately throws an exception if the TVB is truncated.

Earlier, frame_len is computed as
`frame_len = tvb_reported_length_remaining(tvb, 0) - FCOE_HEADER_LEN - FCOE_TRAILER_LEN;`
which can be negative. It should be `frame_len = tvb_reported_length_remaining(tvb, FCOE_HEADER_LEN + FCOE_TRAILER_LEN)`

`proto_tree_add_checksum` takes an unsigned offset (so it casts the negative to a Really Big Positive), but then ends up calling various other `proto_tree_add_item` or `proto_tree_add_uint` functions that cast it back to a negative. I don't think there's *actually* an overrun here, just a warning that it's suspicious because a negative is being cast to a Really Big Positive (even if then cast back to a negative when used.)
But I think changing the `reported_length_remaining()` call would prevent the Coverity issue.
